2608.22504.title: When Does AI for PDEs Yield Scientific Evidence?
2608.22504.paper_summary: Existing AI-for-PDE benchmarks primarily assess models in terms of predictive or approximation accuracy. In physics research, however, AI outputs often serve as evidence for scientific claims. These two objectives are not equivalent: the former measures an output's agreement with a reference target or satisfaction of governing constraints; the latter asks whether, given a specified object of study, scientific claim, assumptions, and evidence standard, the output provides sufficient evidence for that claim. To bridge this gap, we extend a widely used PDE-simulation benchmark and a comprehensive benchmark for PDE inverse problems to enable, for the first time in AI for PDEs, evaluation of whether and to what extent model outputs support specified scientific claims. Our results show that numerical accuracy and evidential support can rank models differently, explain when and why they do so, and reveal that existing benchmarks can favor methods whose outputs provide weaker support for the scientific claims of interest. Together, we formalize, empirically demonstrate, and explain this evaluation--use mismatch in AI for PDEs.
2608.22504.paper_summary_zh: 現有的 AI-for-PDE 基準主要評估模型的預測或近似準確性。然而，在物理研究中，AI 的輸出往往作為科學主張的證據。這兩個目標並不等價：前者衡量輸出與參考目標的一致性或滿足控制約束的程度；後者則詢問在給定特定研究對象、科學主張、假設和證據標準的情況下，輸出是否提供了足夠的證據來支持該主張。為了填補這一空白，我們擴展了一個廣泛使用的 PDE 模擬基準和一個全面的 PDE 反問題基準，以首次在 AI for PDEs 中評估模型輸出是否以及在多大程度上支持特定的科學主張。我們的結果顯示，數值準確性和證據支持可以以不同的方式對模型進行排名，解釋它們何時以及為什麼如此，並揭示現有基準可能偏向那些提供較弱支持的科學主張的方法。總體而言，我們正式化、實證演示並解釋了這一評估——AI for PDEs 中的使用不匹配。
2608.22504.author: Wenshuo Wang et.al.
